title: Spatio-Temporal Graph Few-Shot Learning with Cross-City Knowledge Transfer

problem.claim: Data-scarce developing cities lack sufficient data to train well-performing spatio-temporal graph models for urban computing tasks.

gap.claim: Existing few-shot learning methods are limited by irregular cross-city graph structures and varied features.

contributions.claim: A model-agnostic few-shot learning framework for spatio-temporal graphs, ST-GFSL.
A node-level meta-knowledge mechanism that generates non-shared parameters and transfers knowledge through parameter matching.
A graph reconstruction objective for structure-aware learning during meta-learning.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments were conducted on four traffic speed prediction benchmarks.
The reported results demonstrate effectiveness compared with state-of-the-art methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Spatio-temporal graph learning supports urban computing forecasting tasks.
Developing cities may have too little data to train well-performing models.
Cross-city transfer is promising, but differing graph structures and features constrain existing few-shot methods.
ST-GFSL transfers node-level meta knowledge through parameter matching and reconstructs graph structure during meta-learning.
The authors report evaluations on four traffic speed prediction benchmarks against state-of-the-art methods.

source_observation.claim: Cross-city transfer is challenged by irregular graph structures and varied features.

interpretation.claim: Transfer mechanisms may need to adapt parameters and account for structural differences rather than assume aligned graphs.

application.claim: For few-shot transfer across heterogeneous spatial domains, consider adaptive parameter matching and structure-aware objectives.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these mechanisms generalize beyond the reported traffic speed prediction benchmarks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the four benchmarks, dataset sizes, or city pairs.
The abstract does not report quantitative results, baselines, or statistical details.
The abstract does not describe the meta-learning procedure or parameter-matching algorithm in detail.
